title: Don’t celebrate Easter without change.
paragraphs:
Don’t celebrate Easter without change.
Because an empty tomb means nothing to a heart still in love with disobedience.
James 1:22 hits like a hammer: “But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.”

You can sing resurrection songs.
Wear your Sunday best.
Post the cross.
Say “He is risen.”
And still walk out of church unchanged.

That is not revival.
That is self-deception.

Easter is not a yearly emotional moment.
It is the announcement that Jesus Christ crushed sin, broke death, and rose in power—so we would not stay the same. The risen Christ does not just want your applause. He wants your surrender.

The resurrection is not only proof that Jesus lives.
It is a call for dead things in us to die.
Dead habits.
Secret compromise.
Proud attitudes.
Convenient Christianity.
Performative faith.
If the tomb is empty, your excuses must be too.

Jesus did not rise so you could remain a listener with no obedience. He rose to make sinners new. He rose to call the lukewarm back to fire. He rose to give grace not just to comfort you—but to transform you.

So before you celebrate Easter, ask yourself:
What in me still refuses the Word of God?
What sin am I protecting?
What truth have I heard again and again, but still refused to obey?

This is not condemnation for the broken.
This is an invitation to repentance.

Because the same risen Savior who confronts you also welcomes you.
The same Jesus who exposes sin also washes it.
The same Christ who came out of the grave can pull you out of the life you keep pretending is fine.

Don’t just attend Easter.
Answer it.

Repent.
Believe again.
Obey the Word.
And let resurrection power show up in the way you actually live.

He is risen.
So don’t stay spiritually buried.
